clue.text: US general unwilling to arrange truces?

indicators.note: to arrange the word truces is to put its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: An American general refuses to negotiate any ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the real man, who fought the Plains Indians; 'unwilling' is only a link here, and 'to arrange' rearranges TRUCES.
explanation.definitionFit: George Armstrong Custer was a cavalry commander killed at the Little Bighorn in 1876.

clue.text: Charge old shock trooper

parts.note: to have charge of something is to have command of it

explanation.surface: An elderly soldier leads a fierce assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier trained for raids and surprise attacks is exactly a shock trooper.

clue.text: Stop serving drink to reporters

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
the press is the body of reporters and journalists

explanation.surface: A barman is told to stop serving alcohol to journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down or quash something is to halt it, as when a rebellion is stopped.

clue.text: Constantly veer about

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of veer are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something keeps swinging round all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean always or at all times, as in 'for ever'.

clue.text: Gets a helping hand, though it's denied

parts.note: to gain something is to get it
aid is help or assistance, a helping hand

explanation.surface: Someone receives assistance, but it is officially refused.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so the past tense means contradicted.

clue.text: Work hard to compete in the job market

explanation.surface: Advice to a jobseeker: put your back into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense plays on applying for a job yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To devote effort and concentration is to work hard; making an application for a post is competing for employment.

clue.text: Refusal to be quiet when common food is served

parts.note: no is the word of refusal
sh is the sound used to tell someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone won't stay silent while plain meals are dished out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal, slangy British word for grub or something to eat.

clue.text: Degraded since being put in a retirement place

indicators.note: being put in says the word for since goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a bed is where you go when you retire for the night
as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'

explanation.surface: Someone has been humiliated ever since being sent to an old people's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests old age, but retiring here means going to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humbled or lowered in dignity has been degraded.

clue.text: Expected girl to return to guardian

parts.note: something due is expected, as a train is due at noon

indicators.note: to return means the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is expected to go back to the person looking after her.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone to a young lady, a guardian of her conduct.

clue.text: Baby has a mass of hair, sweetie

parts.note: a mop is a thick untidy mass of hair
pet is a term of endearment like sweetie

explanation.surface: An infant with a shock of hair is called darling.
explanation.definitionFit: A moppet is an endearing small child, a little one.

clue.text: A Lombard banker will declare his defection?

definitions.text: A Lombard banker will declare his defection?

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks, and the Po is the river of Lombardy
to state is to declare

explanation.surface: An Italian financier announces that he is switching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests finance but means a river; the whole clue describes someone who renounces a faith and says so.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade who abandons a religion or cause publicly declares that change of loyalty.

clue.text: Protector commenting adversely on woman's size?

explanation.surface: A guardian makes unkind remarks about a woman's build.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as FAT HER FIGURE, a rude remark on a woman's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A father figure is an older man looked up to for guidance and protection; split differently it calls a lady's shape plump.

clue.text: Sprightly sprite loses her head

indicators.note: loses her head says the first letter of the sprite's name is dropped

parts.note: a sprite is a fairy

explanation.surface: A lively elf is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy can mean light-hearted and lively, like something sprightly.

clue.text: Paints a Tyrolean scene featuring woodland god

indicators.note: a scene featuring something contains it, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: An artist depicts an Alpine landscape with a forest deity in it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a satyr is a goat-legged spirit of the forests, companion of Dionysus.

clue.text: Run up from all directions

parts.note: south is S, one of the four compass points
east is E, another compass point
west is W, another compass point
north is N, the last compass point

explanation.surface: Rushing uphill from everywhere at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run up' is a dressmaking phrase for stitched quickly, not climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up a garment is to stitch it together quickly, so a run-up dress has been stitched.

clue.text: Article Reginald rejected in rage

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: rejected here means turned back, so the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Reg is the short form of Reginald

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is turned down by Reginald in a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage and fury are strong forms of the same emotion.

clue.text: Niggardly skinhead acquires money

parts.note: mean is stingy or niggardly
the head of skin, its first letter, is S

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted thug comes into some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' looks like the thug but is read as skin's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of means has wealth; means are financial resources.

clue.text: Poor Denis sang, despite being disillusioned

indicators.note: poor suggests the name Denis is badly made and must be rearranged

parts.note: to chant is to sing, so chanted means sang

explanation.surface: Denis sang badly even though he had lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' signals an anagram of the name only, giving DISEN; 'despite being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disenchanted is to have lost one's illusions or faith in something.

clue.text: The angler's missus was a harridan

explanation.surface: The fisherman's wife turned out to be a scold.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense jokes on a fisherman's wife; the word really means a coarse, loud-mouthed woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishwife was a woman selling fish, proverbially loud and abusive, so a shrew; a fisherman's spouse is jokingly the same.

clue.text: What political campaigners did when disturbed

explanation.surface: Activists stirred things up when upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to campaign for change; being agitated is being worried or upset.

clue.text: Standing in for a salesman taking offence

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
resenting something is taking offence at it

explanation.surface: A stand-in for a sales agent is getting annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone acting on another's behalf is substituting for them.

clue.text: Couple and daughter are given support

parts.note: a brace is a pair or couple, as of game birds

explanation.surface: Two parents and their daughter receive help.
explanation.definitionFit: Something braced has been propped or strengthened.

clue.text: A greeting that upset mother, unfortunately

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
alas is said when something is unfortunate

explanation.surface: A hello that sadly upset Mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns MAALAS, the two pieces together, from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a low bow with the hand to the forehead, a respectful salutation in Muslim countries.

clue.text: A horse raced round the ring

indicators.note: round says the word for raced goes around the ring's letter

parts.note: ran means raced
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A racehorse galloped round the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse with a coat of mixed white and coloured hairs.

clue.text: Penny having ailments is on medication

parts.note: ills are ailments

explanation.surface: Penny is unwell and taking her tablets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but is P, a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablets swallowed as medicine are a form of treatment.

clue.text: Converse for a short time after church

indicators.note: after says the following letters come behind the abbreviation for church

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Have a brief word once the service is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' signals the abbreviation T for time, not brevity of talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk informally with someone is to converse.

clue.text: Opposed to keeping silver at home

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone objects to storing silver in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against.

clue.text: Not all will display character

explanation.surface: Not everyone shows grit.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is less than the whole; an actor's role in a play is a character.

clue.text: Such commotion initially caused weariness

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of caused

parts.note: langour is lethargy or weariness

explanation.surface: A big disturbance at first left everyone exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangour is a loud ringing din, a noisy uproar.

clue.text: A Christian pious in days gone by

indicators.note: in says the word for pious is placed within the word for days gone by

parts.note: the past is days gone by
pi is an informal word for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A devout believer in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Papist is an old, hostile name for a Roman Catholic.

clue.text: He died in action, it's claimed

indicators.note: in says the man and the died abbreviation go inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
he refers to a male, a man

explanation.surface: A soldier was killed in battle, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In action' looks like a battlefield phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'He' is simply a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand something is to insist on it as a right, much like claiming it.

clue.text: Come and listen

explanation.surface: An invitation to arrive and pay heed.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it; to attend to a speaker is to pay heed.
